dedupe_keys.name: karachi residential electricity consumption on a 30 m grid k electric about 2 million households with ti city accra urban expansion data

description: This UK Data Service collection from the ESRC-funded Quantifying Cities project holds two datasets. The first is residential electricity consumption for Karachi, Pakistan, supplied by K-Electric, the city monopoly electricity provider: average monthly kWh for about 2 million households aggregated into 193,050 grid cells of 30 m, with cell centroids carrying the median of average monthly household consumption, used by the authors to map intra-urban living standards. The second is the input data of the TI-City model of urban expansion in Accra, Ghana, as ASCII files of infrastructure and amenities that shape the location choices of households and developers, gathered from Ghanaian land-use and planning institutions and secondary sources. Temporal coverage is 2000 to 2021, and the collection was published on 3 March 2023. The Karachi file is a 29 MB GeoPackage under the UK Data Service End User Licence, available only on request: all requests need the permission of the data owner through the listed contact. Coverage is Karachi and Accra. Caveats: values are grid-cell medians, not meters, and access depends on owner approval. Simulation uses are fine-grained residential demand maps for distribution planning and equity analysis of electricity access. Related records: none in the catalogue for Karachi yet.
